newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian 88 plans C$100 mln '97 budget.
newsitem.headline: Canadian 88 plans C$100 mln '97 budget.

text.p: Canadian 88 Energy Corp said on Wednesday that it planned to spend C$100 million on exploration and development in 1997, its highest capital budget to date.
Canadian 88 said its 1997 budget would be funded mostly from cash flow and spending would be concentrate in its core operating areas.
The company was expected to ring up a total of C$75 million for capital spending in 1996, Canadian 88 vice-president Geoff Smith said.
Smith said financing for major acquisitions, should opportunities arise, would be aobe the C$100 million budgeted for next year.
The company said results from a huge 3D seismic program shot on its Olds/Crossfield acreage in central Alberta would be available in the first quarter of 1997.
The data was expected to produce new deep horizontal natural gas drilling locations on the lands, it said.
A further expansion of the company's Olds gas plant by 50 million cubic feet per day was also planned for next year. The planned was expanded by 20 MMCFD this year.
Canadian 88 said it planned to drill up to two of five development wells at its much-watched Waterton deep gas discovery in the southern Alberta foothills.
It said construction of a pipeline to link the Waterton discovery to Shell Canada Ltd's Watern plant would start in January.
The 1997 budget also included plans to shoot 2D seismic on Canadian 88's 215,000-acre exploration block in the MacKenzie Valley area of Canada's Northwest Territories, it said.
It said it was considering an exploration test, targeting an oil accumulation, in the second hald of 1997 in the agreage, which is near Norman Wells.

The company said spending, which would be in addition to its own 1997 budget, would also start under its recently established C$150-million Rocky Mountain Energy fund, a three-year joint venture funded by Canadian 88 and a consortium of U.S.-based exploration companies and Canadian institutional investors.
